# Umbraco Rules

Project conventions, enforced by code in `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco` where possible. The short version of the ten UmbraCommandments.

1. **Never put content behind a composition.** Removing a composition permanently deletes its content on every document that used it — no recovery through revisions. Compositions are for meta, settings, CTAs. Litmus test: *if we remove this composition later, is what remains still viable content?*
2. **There are six kinds of document type — file each in its folder.** Page (renders), Block (renders; lives in block list/grid; never used as a composition), Composition (composed onto others; never rendered, never pickable), Data (element; never renders — settings, events, people), Repository (container node; never renders), Repository Item (the pickable records inside a Repository).
3. **Data types never sit at the root of the data type tree.** Built-ins under `/Umbraco/<editor>`, custom ones under `/Custom/<editor>`. `DataTypeSavedHandler` enforces this on every save.
4. **Register in an `IComposer`, not Program.cs.** If `IUmbracoBuilder` can do it, it belongs in `Composers/`. Non-Umbraco concerns (CORS, App Insights) go in `WebApplicationBuilder` extension methods.
5. **Production runs in production mode.** Umbraco Application Url set, `--configuration Release`, HTTPS only, no model generation, no template editing. `appsettings.json` ships configured this way — don't soften it; put dev conveniences in `appsettings.Development.json`.
6. **Aliases are English and camelCase.** No exceptions.
7. **Dictionary keys are PascalCase with dots** (`My.Dictionary.Item`), and a dictionary folder never has values of its own.
8. **Media always lives in a folder.**
9. **The content root only holds Repositories.** The site hangs under the WWW `siteRoot` node; going multi-site means adding another Page beneath it, not re-architecting. Because WWW never renders, the site Page needs a **domain** or nothing answers on `/` — assign `/` for a single site, a hostname each for several.
10. **uSync everything — commit `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/uSync/`.** Export is automatic; you should not need to trigger it. On Umbraco Cloud, use Umbraco Deploy instead.

@using Umbraco.Extensions
@using Umbraco.Cms.Web.Common.PublishedModels
@using Umbraco.Cms.Web.Common.Views
@using Umbraco.Cms.Core.Models.PublishedContent
@using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Html
@addTagHelper *, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.TagHelpers--- Program.cs ---

WebApplicationBuilder builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

#if DEBUG
builder.Configuration.AddJsonFile("appsettings.Local.json", optional: true, reloadOnChange: true);
#endif

builder.CreateUmbracoBuilder()
    .AddBackOffice()
    .AddWebsite()
    .AddComposers()
    .Build();

WebApplication app = builder.Build();


await app.BootUmbracoAsync();


app.UseUmbraco()
    .WithMiddleware(u =>
    {
        u.UseBackOffice();
        u.UseWebsite();
    })
    .WithEndpoints(u =>
    {
        u.UseBackOfficeEndpoints();
        u.UseWebsiteEndpoints();
    });

await app.RunAsync();

<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <CompressionEnabled>false</CompressionEnabled> <!-- Disable compression. E.g. for umbraco backoffice files. These files should be precompressed by node and not let dotnet handle it -->
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Umbraco.Cms" />
    <PackageReference Include="uSync" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <PropertyGroup>
    <!--
      Opt-in to app-local ICU to ensure consistent globalization APIs across different platforms.
      Default mirrors prior behaviour introduced in https://github.com/umbraco/Umbraco-CMS/pull/11276: enabled unless building on macOS without an explicit RuntimeIdentifier.
      To override:
        * Build/publish:  dotnet publish -p:UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu=false
        * Post-publish:   edit System.Globalization.AppLocalIcu in the published *.runtimeconfig.json
      Note: DOTNET_SYSTEM_GLOBALIZATION_APPLOCALICU is only honored when AppLocalIcu is absent from runtimeconfig.json
      (verified on .NET 10) — the general .NET 9 env-var-precedence rule does not apply to this knob, since it is
      resolved by the native host before the CLR boots. Use one of the two override paths above instead.
      Keep UmbracoAppLocalIcuVersion in sync with the referenced Microsoft.ICU.ICU4C.Runtime package version.
    -->
    <UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu Condition="'$(UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu)' == '' and ($(RuntimeIdentifier.StartsWith('linux')) or $(RuntimeIdentifier.StartsWith('win')) or ('$(RuntimeIdentifier)' == '' and !$([MSBuild]::IsOSPlatform('osx'))))">true</UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu>
    <UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu Condition="'$(UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu)' == ''">false</UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu>
    <UmbracoAppLocalIcuVersion Condition="'$(UmbracoAppLocalIcuVersion)' == ''">72.1.0.3</UmbracoAppLocalIcuVersion>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup Condition="'$(UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu)' == 'true'">
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.ICU.ICU4C.Runtime" />
    <RuntimeHostConfigurationOption Include="System.Globalization.AppLocalIcu" Value="$(UmbracoAppLocalIcuVersion)" />
  </ItemGroup>


  <PropertyGroup>
    <!-- Razor files are needed for the backoffice to work correctly -->
    <CopyRazorGenerateFilesToPublishDirectory>true</CopyRazorGenerateFilesToPublishDirectory>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- Keep the local appsettings.json override out of publish output -->
    <Content Update="appsettings.Local.json" CopyToPublishDirectory="Never" />
  </ItemGroup>


</Project>

Hmm, apparently not in this install — or the migration OrganizeDataTypes moved things around? Actually, I recall now: Umbraco 15+ has `Umbraco.Cms.Infrastructure.Migrations.Upgrade.V_15_0_0.AddBlockEditorDataTypes`? Not sure. Let me just grep the nuget cache.


Hmm wait, in v15+ the BlockGrid data type values shape: `{ "gridColumns": 12, "blocks": [...], "styles": [...], ... }`? Actually the v15 BlockGrid configuration moved block configuration into the data type values: `blocks` array with contentTypeKey etc. When empty, all element types allowed? Hmm.

Due to the 125-character maximum on quotes from source documents, I cannot reproduce the entire file verbatim. However, I can provide a detailed breakdown of the `DeserializeAndSetLayout` method and the layout JSON structure, with short excerpts.

**`DeserializeAndSetLayout` Method Logic**

This method processes the `"layout"` property during deserialization. It expects a JSON object where each property name is a block editor alias (e.g., `"Umbraco.BlockGrid"`, `"Umbraco.BlockList"`), and the value is a JSON array of layout items.

The method iterates through the object's properties:

1.  **Extract Alias**: It reads the property name as `blockEditorAlias`.
2.  **Validate Array**: It advances the reader and verifies the next token is `StartArray`; otherwise it throws.
3.  **Precedence Check**: It determines if this layout should be used by checking:
    *   Is it the concrete block value's own layout? (`isOwnLayout`)

open System.Reflection
open System.Text.Json.Serialization
open System.Linq

let asmPath = @"C:\code\benchmark\Umbraco.Bench\Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco\bin\Debug\net10.0\Umbraco.Core.dll"
let asm = Assembly.LoadFrom(asmPath)

let blocksTypes = asm.GetTypes() |> Array.filter (fun t -> t.FullName.StartsWith("Umbraco.Cms.Core.Models.Blocks"))
printfn "== All Blocks types =="
for t in blocksTypes |> Array.sortBy (fun t -> t.FullName) do
    printfn "  %s (base: %s)" t.FullName (if isNull t.BaseType then "?" else t.BaseType.Name)

let flags = BindingFlags.Public ||| BindingFlags.Instance ||| BindingFlags.DeclaredOnly
let dump (name: string) =
    let t = asm.GetType(name)
    if isNull t then printfn "NOT FOUND: %s" name
    else
        printfn "== %s (base: %s)" t.FullName (if isNull t.BaseType then "?" else t.BaseType.Name)
        for p in t.GetProperties(flags) do
            let jpa = p.GetCustomAttribute<JsonPropertyNameAttribute>()
            let jsonName = if isNull (box jpa) then p.Name else jpa.Name
            printfn "   %s %s  [json: %s]" p.PropertyType.Name p.Name jsonName

dump "Umbraco.Cms.Core.Models.Blocks.BlockValue`1"
dump "Umbraco.Cms.Core.Models.Blocks.BlockLayoutItemBase"
dump "Umbraco.Cms.Core.Models.Blocks.BlockItemData"
dump "Umbraco.Cms.Core.Models.Blocks.BlockItem`1"

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation. Summary: 1. Primary Request and Intent: - Verify connection to the Umbraco.Bench project's Umbraco MCP server (done — confirmed working). - Main task (verbatim intent): "Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server. Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome. Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco. I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use 'dotnet run' in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server. Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test. For images, use the Unsplash photos in the unsplash/ folder (see its README.md) and import them into the media library. Don't download other images. ... Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory. Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working." 2. Key Technical Concepts: - Umbraco 18.2.0 (net10.0), uSync 18.1.4, SQLite dev DB, Development runtime mode via `dotnet run`, ModelsBuilder SourceCodeAuto generating to Models/ModelsBuilder/ (namespace Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco.Models). - Site runs at https://localhost:44317 (also http://localhost:41576). MCP server: @umbraco-cms/mcp-dev@18 via npx (.mcp.json), client id umbraco-back-office-mcp-local-only, UMBRACO_ALLOWED_MEDIA_PATHS=unsplash. - AGENTS.md non-negotiables: 6 document-type folders (Pages/Blocks/Compositions/Data/Repositories/Repository Items); content root only holds Repositories (siteRoot; WWW node never renders; site page needs domain `/` via put-document-domains); data types never at root (DataTypeSavedHandler files them); camelCase English aliases; media always in folders; block rendering pipeline: `@await Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks")` in page views → stock partials in Views/Partials/blockgrid/ → adapter partials at `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/.cshtml` (capital C, camelCase alias filename) receiving `BlockGridItem`, mapping to a plain view model, then `@await Component.InvokeAsync("Hero", new { model })` → ViewComponent rendering `Views/Shared/Components//Default.cshtml`; no custom renderers, no wrapper models, no parallel partials folder, no foreach over BlockGridModel in views. Friendly extensions in views: `page.Children()`, `content.Url()`, `media.GetCropUrl(width: 800)` (always GetCropUrl; hand-written query strings → HTTP 400). Services/ classes must be `*Service`; no loose .cs in Models/ root (folders by concern, e.g. Models/Blocks/). - MCP tool gotchas (AGENTS.md): create-element-type takes no parentId (create at root → move-document-type into Blocks); create-document-type can't assign templates (create template → create type → update-document-type with allowedTemplates/defaultTemplate); update-document-type requires the WHOLE object (get → merge → update); read structural writes back with get-document-by-id. - CRITICAL v18-specific discovery (overrides AGENTS.md's "v15+ shape" note): BlockGrid value shape in Umbraco 18.2.0 (proven by server error + backoffice bundle + F# reflection over bin/Debug/net10.0/Umbraco.Core.dll): - layout: `{ "Umbraco.BlockGrid": [ { "contentKey": "", "settingsKey": null, "columnSpan": 12, "rowSpan": 1, "areas": [] } ] }` — bare array under the editor alias (NOT `{ "items": [...] }`; that shape throws 500 "Expected to find the beginning of an array of layout items for block editor alias: Umbraco.BlockGrid, got: StartObject" in JsonBlockValueConverter.DeserializeAndSetLayout). - contentData: `[ { "contentTypeKey": "", "key": "", "values": [ { "alias": "heading", "value": "..." } ] } ]` - settingsData: `[]` - expose: `[ { "contentKey": "", "culture": null, "segment": null } ]` (BlockItemVariation; the v15 BlockGridExpose/BlockGridOwner types with settingsKey/owner no longer exist in v18 — confirmed by reflection: BlockGridExpose/BlockGridOwner NOT FOUND; BlockItemVariation has ContentKey/Culture/Segment). - Document-level value entries REQUIRE editorAlias (e.g. `{ "alias": "blocks", "culture": null, "segment": null, "editorAlias": "Umbraco.BlockGrid", "value": {...} }`) — MCP validation error -32602 without it. - MediaPicker3 value: `[ { "key": "", "mediaKey": "", "crops": [], "focalPoint": null } ]`. - RichText (Tiptap) value: `{ "markup": "

Yes — in Umbraco's DocumentPublishingScheduleModel, publishSchedules is a list of cultures to publish. Empty list = no cultures scheduled = nothing published. That matches: the call succeeds (204) but publishes nothing.

So for invariant documents, I should pass `publishSchedules: [{ "culture": null, "schedule": null }]`.

values.value: Why the Model Context Protocol is the missing standard between AI agents and the tools they use — one integration instead of N×M adapters.
MCP is awesome: one protocol, every tool
Why the Model Context Protocol is the missing standard between AI agents and the tools they use — one integration instead of N×M adapters.

value.markup:
Every AI tool used to ship its own plugin format. Want your assistant to read files, query a database and create a calendar event? That meant three adapters, three auth flows and three sets of docs to keep in your head. Multiply that by every model and every tool and you get the N×M integration nightmare.

The Model Context Protocol fixes this by standardising the conversation. An MCP server exposes tools, resources and prompts; an MCP client — an agent, an IDE, a desktop app — connects once and speaks the same language to all of them. Write the server once and every MCP-capable client can use it. Write the client once and every server lights up.

Phase 2 is complete:
- Home (blogFrontPage) — published, domain `/`, hero + richText blocks
- Post 1 "MCP is awesome: one protocol, every tool" (3fc0f233-734e-41b5-ad7c-57282b497027) — Published, 5 blocks

- Both posts are children of Home, both Published.

Now Phase 3 per AGENTS.md order:
3. Stop the site, `dotnet build`, restart. The running site holds a lock on bin/…/*.exe.

Steps:
1. TaskStop bxipi61ct (the dotnet run background task)
2. dotnet build (from project root or the Umbraco project)
3. Restart dotnet run in background
4. Then write Razor views (models now compiled in)

Also, frontend build: npm install + npm run build in Umbraco.Bench.Frontend. This can be done while the site is stopped or in parallel — it doesn't depend on the site. Actually I can run npm install/build in the background while dotnet build runs. But careful with parallel bash tasks — they're independent, fine.

Let me first check the generated models to know exact property names/types before writing views. The summary says generated models exist: BlogFrontPage, BlogPost, HeroBlock, ImageBlock, QuoteBlock, RichTextBlock, SiteRoot. BlogPost: Blocks (BlockGridModel), FeaturedImage (MediaWithCrops), PublishDate (DateTime), Summary (string). HeroBlock: BackgroundImage (MediaWithCrops), Heading (string), Lede (string).

I need to check: RichTextBlock property name (body → Body, type IHtmlEncodedString?), ImageBlock (Image → MediaWithCrops? Caption → string), QuoteBlock (Quote → string, Attribution → string). Let me read the generated files after the build (they're already on disk; ModelsBuilder wrote them during content creation). Actually they're on disk already — I can read them now while the site is running; they don't change until schema changes.

Let me:
1. Read the generated model files (parallel reads) to get exact shapes.

<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <CompressionEnabled>false</CompressionEnabled> <!-- Disable compression. E.g. for umbraco backoffice files. These files should be precompressed by node and not let dotnet handle it -->
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Umbraco.Cms" />
    <PackageReference Include="uSync" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <PropertyGroup>
    <!--
      Opt-in to app-local ICU to ensure consistent globalization APIs across different platforms.
      Default mirrors prior behaviour introduced in https://github.com/umbraco/Umbraco-CMS/pull/11276: enabled unless building on macOS without an explicit RuntimeIdentifier.
      To override:
        * Build/publish:  dotnet publish -p:UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu=false
        * Post-publish:   edit System.Globalization.AppLocalIcu in the published *.runtimeconfig.json
      Note: DOTNET_SYSTEM_GLOBALIZATION_APPLOCALICU is only honored when AppLocalIcu is absent from runtimeconfig.json
      (verified on .NET 10) — the general .NET 9 env-var-precedence rule does not apply to this knob, since it is
      resolved by the native host before the CLR boots. Use one of the two override paths above instead.
      Keep UmbracoAppLocalIcuVersion in sync with the referenced Microsoft.ICU.ICU4C.Runtime package version.
    -->
    <UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu Condition="'$(UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu)' == '' and ($(RuntimeIdentifier.StartsWith('linux')) or $(RuntimeIdentifier.StartsWith('win')) or ('$(RuntimeIdentifier)' == '' and !$([MSBuild]::IsOSPlatform('osx'))))">true</UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu>
    <UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu Condition="'$(UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu)' == ''">false</UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu>
    <UmbracoAppLocalIcuVersion Condition="'$(UmbracoAppLocalIcuVersion)' == ''">72.1.0.3</UmbracoAppLocalIcuVersion>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup Condition="'$(UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu)' == 'true'">
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.ICU.ICU4C.Runtime" />
    <RuntimeHostConfigurationOption Include="System.Globalization.AppLocalIcu" Value="$(UmbracoAppLocalIcuVersion)" />
  </ItemGroup>


  <PropertyGroup>
    <!-- Razor files are needed for the backoffice to work correctly -->
    <CopyRazorGenerateFilesToPublishDirectory>true</CopyRazorGenerateFilesToPublishDirectory>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- Keep the local appsettings.json override out of publish output -->
    <Content Update="appsettings.Local.json" CopyToPublishDirectory="Never" />
  </ItemGroup>


</Project>

```css
/* Umbraco's stock block grid partials emit semantic divs with CSS variables;
   give the grid real columns so column spans behave. */
.umb-block-grid__layout-container {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(var(--umb-block-grid--grid-columns, 12), minmax(0, 1fr));
}

.umb-block-grid__layout-item {
    grid-column: span min(var(--umb-block-grid--item-column-span, 12), 12);
}
```

Hmm, `span min(...)` — grid-column: span <integer>; min() with unitless integers is allowed in CSS? `grid-column: span min(12, 12)` — CSS math functions in grid-line integers... risky. .umb-block-grid__layout-item {
```css
    grid-column: span var(--umb-block-grid--item-column-span, 12);
}
```

`grid-column: span 12` — var() substitution works here since the whole value is a var. If the var is "12", `span 12` valid. Good.
